name: Every Day I Write the Book

podcast.body: Featured on the album "Punch the Clock," this song became Elvis Costello's only significant Top 40 single in North America during the 1980s. Its success highlighted a period when he was often working solo in the studio, while still using The Attractions for live performances. "From punch the clock, a top 40 North American single called Every Day Are Breakable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.body: Inspired by a ditty from his friend Nick Lowe titled "When I Write The Book," Costello adapted the title into his own song featuring a wickedly catchy piano hook and chanting female backing vocals. Accompanied by a cheeky music video depicting celebrity lookalikes of Prince Charles and Princess Diana navigating domestic life, the song took off on MTV and the charts, becoming Costello's first single to crack the Hot 100 (debuting at #38, peaking at #36) and the Top 40, as well as reaching number 33 on the Rock Tracks chart. "Every day, I write the book, finally changed that."
